article.headline: Robinson scores career-high 23 points to lift No. 6 UCLA over Georgetown, 75-63
article.description: — Sophomore guard Azavier Robinson scored a career-high 23 points off the bench for No. 6 UCLA, which rebounded from its first loss of the season to beat Georgetown 75-63 Friday in the third-place game at the Rady Children's Invitational on Friday.
article.linkText: Robinson scores career-high 23 points to lift No. 6 UCLA over Georgetown, 75-63

article.story: SAN DIEGO -- — Sophomore guard Azavier Robinson scored a career-high 23 points off the bench for No. 6 UCLA, which rebounded from its first loss of the season to beat Georgetown 75-63 Friday in the third-place game at the Rady Children's Invitational on Friday. Eric Dailey Jr. added 14 while Jaylen Petty and Xavier Booker had 10 apiece for UCLA (7-1). The Bruins played more aggressively than they did on Thursday, when they had the lead just once and allowed 15 3-pointers in an 85-70 loss to Saint Mary’s. UCLA took the lead on Dailey's 3-pointer less than four minutes in and never surrendered it. Robinson made consecutive shots early in the first half, the second one off a steal. He had another steal for an easy score midway through the second half. He got a nice ovation as he was subbed out for a breather with the Bruins leading 71-59 with 2:27 to play. Robinson's previous career high was 15 against Arkansas-Pine Bluff on Nov. 11. The Bruins forced the Hoyas into poor shooting from early on. The Hoyas made only 6 of 23 shots in the first half for 26.1%, and just 18 of 52 overall for 34.6%. UCLA shot only 36.1% in the first half and finished at 40.6 percent, but the Bruins outrebounded the Hoyas 43-32 Elmarco Jackson scored 13 for Georgetown (6-2) while Kayvaun Mulready and Caleb Williams had 11 each. The Hoyas lost 92-83 to No. 7 Texas on Thursday. Up next Georgetown: Hosts UMass Lowell on Wednesday night. UCLA: Hosts Oregon in to open Big Ten conference play on Tuesday night. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full men’s basketball coverage here
